caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001777
attempts.entry_title: Tonic GABA and its dopaminergic modulation in the SNr (Simmons et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's slice pharmacology held up in this data: quinpirole reduced the GPe-evoked IPSC in SNr neurons, gabazine no longer changed SNr firing after ALDH1A1 knockdown, ALDH or MAO-B inhibition or GAT-1 block, and astrocytic Gi-DREADD activation and NNC-711 raised firing. The tonic gabazine effect and the slowing by the GAT-3 antagonist SNAP-5114 were significant but about half the paper's size or less. Quinpirole did not raise basal SNr firing or significantly weaken GPe train inhibition, and the paper does not say which cells form its quinpirole group. GPe Gi-DREADD lowered the evoked IPSC in all 4 cells, but not significantly. The SNc, imaging and several drug experiments are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the slice electrophysiology findings of Simmons et al. (2026) on dandiset 001777, which holds cell-attached recordings of SNr neurons before and after bath drugs and whole-cell evoked IPSCs. It compares spike rates and IPSC amplitudes across quinpirole, gabazine, DREADD, ALDH1A1 knockdown and inhibitors, rasagiline and GABA transporter blockers. The SNc recordings, imaging, RNAscope and voltammetry of the paper are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Simmons et al. (2026) from dandiset 001777

outcomes.statement: The D2R agonist quinpirole (2 uM) reduces the amplitude of optogenetically evoked GPe IPSCs in SNr neurons by roughly 30%.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists inhibited phasic GABA release from GPe terminals, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
outcomes.quote: Quinpirole reduced the amplitude of the GPe evoked inhibitory postsynaptic currents (IPSCs) by roughly 30% (P = 0.02 and n = 5)
outcomes.notes: In the 5 labelled cells the first evoked IPSC falls from 265.6 to 198.5 pA in quinpirole, paired t test P = 0.0087; the reduction is 30.1% as the mean of the cells' changes (reading a of M2), 25.3% of the group means and 27.3% as the median. With the sixth cell (second cell of subject 9019, files labelled by an assumed layout) P = 0.0070 and 26.7%. Light pulses at 0.55 s + k x 50 ms are read from the responses, which start 1.2 to 2.2 ms after 0.55 s in every cell. Each of the nine files of that sixth cell, 0015 to 0023, holds an evoked current of 200 to 246 pA, so none was recorded in gabazine; files 0015 to 0018 are 5 min apart and 10 min pass before 0019, which fits the assumed layout.
deviations: The notes of the second IPSC cell of subject 9019 (files 0015 to 0023) are copies of the first cell's and do not say which files are in quinpirole; the cell is left out of the main test and shown as a variant with files 15 to 18 as control and 19 to 22 as quinpirole, the first cell's layout.
The light pulses are not stored in the files; their times are read from the evoked currents.

The notes give holding potentials of -70, -50 and -55 mV for these cells (the paper, -60 mV); the currents are inward in the cell at -70 mV and outward in the others, so the amplitude is the peak deflection with its sign fixed by the cell's control.
Peak window 0.5 to 20 ms after the pulse and baseline the 20 ms before it, a standard choice that the claims file leaves open.

outcomes.statement: The optically evoked GPe currents in SNr neurons are blocked by the GABAA receptor antagonist gabazine (10 uM).
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists inhibited phasic GABA release from GPe terminals, paragraph 1; Figure 1B
outcomes.quote: These optically evoked currents were blocked by bath application of the GABAA receptor (GABAAR) antagonist gabazine (10 μM).
outcomes.notes: None of the 45 optogenetic IPSC files names gabazine in its notes (only quinpirole), and no other file holds evoked IPSCs in gabazine.

outcomes.statement: Quinpirole raises the paired-pulse ratio of GPe evoked IPSCs at a 50 ms interval, consistent with a presynaptic site of action.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists inhibited phasic GABA release from GPe terminals, paragraph 1; Figure 1D and 1E
outcomes.quote: Consistent with a presynaptic locus of the ... the paired-pulse ratio of GPe evoked IPSCs rose in the presence of quinpirole (P = 0.02 and n = 6)
outcomes.notes: The paired-pulse ratio (second over first IPSC, 50 ms apart) rises in 5 of 5 labelled cells, from 0.868 to 0.897 (reading a, paired t test P = 0.022) and from 0.861 to 0.889 (reading b, P = 0.013). With the sixth cell (the paper's n = 6) it rises in 6 of 6 (P = 0.010 and 0.011).
deviations: The sixth cell rests on the assumed file layout described under fig1c-quinpirole-reduces-gpe-ipsc; the outcome is the same with and without it.

outcomes.statement: A 2-s, 30-Hz optogenetic train of GPe inputs inhibits SNr spiking, and quinpirole attenuates this inhibition.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists inhibited phasic GABA release from GPe terminals, paragraph 2; Figure 2A to 2C
outcomes.quote: quinpirole attenuated the ability of GPe stimulation to slow the spiking of SNr neurons (P = 0.02 and n = 8)
outcomes.notes: Percent inhibition (basal minus train rate over basal, from each condition's PSTH) falls from 56.8 to 42.3 in quinpirole over the 8 cells (basal 0 to 2 s), less inhibition in 5 of 8, Wilcoxon P = 0.11 (one-sided 0.055). Basal 0 to 2 s with 4 to 6 s gives 58.6 against 43.7, P = 0.11; the same at thresholds 6 and 12. The per-sweep median variant gives P = 0.15 at thresholds 8 and 12 and 0.11 at 6. Under reading b of M1 (quinpirole sweeps from 6 min) the inhibition in quinpirole is 37.1 and P = 0.078 to 0.11 at every threshold and basal window (one-sided 0.039 to 0.055). The direction matches the paper; no two-sided test reaches P < 0.05.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.
All sweeps of each condition form its PSTH; the paper's code chooses the episodes by eye.

outcomes.statement: The GPe train initially suppresses SNr spiking strongly, and the inhibition wanes during the 2-s train.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists inhibited phasic GABA release from GPe terminals, paragraph 2; Figure 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: this stimulation effectively suppressed SNr activity, but the efficacy of this inhibition waned with time (Fig. 2, A to C)
outcomes.notes: In the control PSTH pooled over the 8 cells the rate is 4.26 Hz in 2.0 to 2.5 s and 11.85 Hz in 3.5 to 4.0 s; the last window is higher in 8 of 8 cells, at every threshold. The train timing (2 to 4 s) is shown in the data: control rates fall from 7.7 to 50.3 Hz before the train to 0.2 to 24.9 Hz in its first 0.2 s in the Chronos cells, and do not fall in the cells without an opsin.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.

outcomes.statement: Quinpirole alone, with no GPe stimulation, raises the basal spike rate of SNr neurons, by about 50% in cell-attached recordings.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists lowered tonic GABA release, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: One of the unexpected observations in these experiments was the ... in the basal spiking rate of SNr neurons with bath application of quinpirole, in the absence of GPe axon stimulation (P < 0.01 and n = 8) (Fig. 3A). The quinpirole-induced elevation in discharge rate was about 50% when monitored in cell-attached mode.
outcomes.notes: Two sets of cells fit the paper's description and both were run. (i) 7 cells without an opsin recorded with the same protocol: 24.8 to 21.0 Hz, paired t test P = 0.30 (reading b 20.2 Hz, P = 0.20), a decrease. (ii) The 8 Chronos cells of Fig. 2, rate over 0 to 2 s before the train: 20.2 to 24.9 Hz, +31.8% (mean of cells), P = 0.24; reading b +43.2%, P = 0.20. No paired t test gives P < 0.05 under any reading or threshold; the paper reports P < 0.01 and about 50%. The dataset holds 7 cells in set (i) against the paper's 8. One of them, 5110-2020-10-20-15, is a failed recording (its action currents shrink into the noise, falling from 18.5 to 9.8 noise units during the control file); without it the 6 cells give 25.1 against 24.5 Hz, P = 0.53 (reading b -8.9%, P = 0.079).
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.

The paper says the rise was seen 'in these experiments' (the Fig. 2 recordings) 'in the absence of GPe axon stimulation' (Results, D2R agonists lowered tonic GABA release, paragraph 1); which cells form its n = 8 is not stated, so both sets are run.

Seven cell-attached recordings lose their action currents during the experiment (the rate falls under a quarter of the condition before, a limit chosen here, and the spike amplitude falls to the noise). They are kept in the main test, as the claims file asks for every cell, and the test is also run without them.

outcomes.statement: Gabazine raises the basal spike rate of SNr neurons by roughly 25%, which the paper reads as a tonic inhibition through GABAA receptors.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists lowered tonic GABA release, paragraph 1; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: gabazine (10 μM) increased the basal spiking rate of SNr ... recorded in cell-attached mode by roughly 25%, suggesting that they were tonically inhibited by activation of GABAARs (P < 0.01 and n = 10)

statistics.about: as given in the Figure 3B legend

outcomes.notes: Over the 49 gabazine-alone cells (25 subjects; the paper gives n = 10 in the Results and 45 in the legend) gabazine raises the rate from 21.4 to 23.2 Hz under reading b (paired t test P = 0.047, Wilcoxon P = 0.0044) and to 22.5 Hz under reading a (P = 0.19, Wilcoxon P = 0.023); 31 of 49 cells are faster. The increase is 9.5%, 8.2% and 12.0% (readings a, b, c of M2, reading b of M1), against 25 +/- 2.5%. With the gap-free files measured in the windows their notes give (the other cells as reading a): +9.1%, P = 0.065; the gap-free cells on their own, as reading a, give P = 0.20. At threshold 12 no paired t test gives P < 0.05. Two of the 49 are failed recordings (7310-2023-01-06-84 and 7324-2023-02-22-93, whose action currents shrink into the noise in gabazine); without them the rise is significant under both readings at thresholds 6 and 8 (reading a P = 0.0097, reading b P = 0.0014 at 8) and is 10.8%, 7.7% and 8.9% (reading a of M1) or 14.2%, 11.2% and 13.5% (reading b). Under reading a of M1 with all 49 cells the increase is 6.3%, 4.9% and 8.8% at threshold 8, a fifth to a third of the paper's size, and 5.1%, 1.6% and 8.0% at 12. The notes of 8945-2025-04-16-144 say gabazine was applied during its control file; its rate there is 23.5 Hz before the end of the noted baseline window and 23.3 Hz after, and without it reading b gives P = 0.048 at threshold 8.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.
49 cells against the paper's 45; the paper does not say which cells form its n.

Assumed: the P < 0.05 part rests on the detection threshold. With all 49 cells it holds only at thresholds 6 and 8 under reading b of M1 (P = 0.035 and 0.047), and at no threshold under reading a; without the two failed recordings it holds under both readings at 6 and 8. At threshold 12 no paired test with all 49 cells is significant. Threshold 8 is the main reading because it falls in the gap between noise crossings and action currents in most files (data check).

Seven cell-attached recordings lose their action currents during the experiment (the rate falls under a quarter of the condition before, a limit chosen here, and the spike amplitude falls to the noise). They are kept in the main test, as the claims file asks for every cell, and the test is also run without them.

outcomes.statement: In the presence of gabazine, quinpirole does not change SNr spike rate.
outcomes.source: Results, D2R agonists lowered tonic GABA release, paragraph 1; Figure 3D (the Results cite it as Fig. 3C, which is the map of gabazine-treated cells)
outcomes.quote: Indeed, in the presence of gabazine, quinpirole did not modulate SNr spiking rate (P = 0.13 and n = 7)

statistics.about: as given in the Figure 3D legend

outcomes.notes: No file's notes describe quinpirole applied in gabazine; the quinpirole recordings are the Fig. 2 cells, the cells without an opsin, and SNAP-5114 then quinpirole.

outcomes.statement: The increase in SNr spike rate with gabazine is weakly and positively correlated with the basal rate.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Summary data and linear regression of a weak positive correlation between basal discharge rate and the effect of gabazine R2 = 0.11, n = 39
outcomes.notes: Over the 49 gabazine-alone cells the change in rate is unrelated to the basal rate: R2 = 0.004, slope -0.033 (reading a) and R2 = 0.004, slope 0.037 (reading b); R2 is at most 0.009 at any threshold. The paper reports R2 = 0.11 with a positive slope over 39 cells, which the dataset does not identify. Without the two failed recordings (47 cells) R2 is at most 0.028, and the slope is negative under reading a.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.

Seven cell-attached recordings lose their action currents during the experiment (the rate falls under a quarter of the condition before, a limit chosen here, and the spike amplitude falls to the noise). They are kept in the main test, as the claims file asks for every cell, and the test is also run without them.

outcomes.statement: Activating Gi-DREADD in GPe with CNO reduces the amplitude of electrically evoked IPSCs in SNr neurons, similar in size to the quinpirole effect on optogenetically evoked IPSCs.
outcomes.source: Results, Tonic GABA release was not derived from GPe terminals or astrocytes, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
outcomes.quote: Bath application of the DREADD agonist clozapine-N-oxide (CNO) reduced the ... of electrically evoked IPSCs in voltage-clamped SNr neurons (P = 0.02 and n = 4) (Fig. 4A). This modulation was similar in ... to that seen in optogenetically evoked IPSCs following D2R stimulation.

statistics.about: as given in the Figure 4A legend

outcomes.notes: Four cells, one electrical pulse at 0.40 s per 1-s sweep. Spontaneous action currents fall into 23 and 18 CNO sweeps of two cells and 89 of the 100 control sweeps of 6921-2022-09-28-60; they are found as high-passed deflections over 50 noise units (clean sweeps stay under 50, action currents mostly over 100). On the mean of the clean sweeps, the claims file's measure, the amplitude falls in 4 of 4 cells, from 73.1 to 37.5 pA, by 48.7% (mean of cells), 48.7% (of means) and 54.5% (median), paired t test P = 0.11 (one-sided 0.056); with the limit at 100 noise units P = 0.12 and 46.4 to 49.6%. The reductions are 16 points or more from the 30.1% of fig1c, outside the 10-point margin. On the mean of all sweeps the amplitude rises in 2 of 4 (P = 0.42); on the median of sweeps it falls by 42.5% (P = 0.13). The current of 6921-2022-09-28-60 is outward in its 11 clean control sweeps, where the other three cells at -60 mV are inward. Neither part of the criterion is met.
deviations: The protocol is named 'Five stim 25Hz' but the sweeps hold one pulse at 0.40 s; the IPSC after it is measured 3 to 20 ms after the pulse, past the stimulus artifact.

The mean is taken over the sweeps without a spontaneous action current (a 300 Hz high-passed deflection over 50 noise units outside the stimulus artifact, a limit chosen here where the clean and contaminated sweeps separate; 100 is shown as a variant), and the sign of each cell's current is fixed from its clean control sweeps. The mean of all sweeps and the median of sweeps are variants.

outcomes.statement: Inhibiting GPe terminals with Gi-DREADD does not change the basal spike rate of SNr neurons, which the paper takes as evidence that GPe terminals do not contribute to tonic GABA release.
outcomes.source: Results, Tonic GABA release was not derived from GPe terminals or astrocytes, paragraph 1; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: However, CNO application had no effect on the basal spiking rate of SNr neurons recorded in cell-attached mode, arguing that GPe terminals were not contributing to tonic GABA release (P = 0.19 and n = 5)

statistics.about: as given in the Figure 4B legend

outcomes.notes: In the 5 cells CNO gives 21.9 against 15.1 Hz, paired t test P = 0.27 (reading b P = 0.23), and P >= 0.12 under both readings at thresholds 6 and 8; the rate falls in 3 of 5, one cell from 55.3 to 27.5 Hz. At threshold 12, reading b gives P = 0.036, a decrease (reading a P = 0.11). Two cells depend on the threshold: 6917-2022-08-29-58 fires at 55 to 57 Hz in control at thresholds 6 and 8 and 28.6 Hz at 12, and at 27.5 Hz in CNO at 8, so at 8 its two conditions are not counted alike; at threshold 12 most spikes of 6887-2022-07-14-57 are missed (6.5 and 0.42 Hz against 16.5 Hz at 6 and 8). Under reading a P is 0.11 to 0.27 at every threshold, so the absence holds at all three (M1, a claim holds under either reading); the one significant result, reading b at threshold 12, comes from the spikes of 6887-2022-07-14-57 missed at that threshold.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.

outcomes.statement: Activating Gq-DREADD in SNr astrocytes with CNO raises the basal spike rate of SNr neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Tonic GABA release was not derived from GPe terminals or astrocytes, paragraph 2; Figure S4B
outcomes.quote: In these slices, bath ... of the DREADD agonist CNO elevated the basal spiking rate of SNr neurons recorded in cell-attached mode (P = 0.03 and n = 8)
outcomes.notes: No file's notes name a Gq-DREADD (hM3) virus; the GFAP virus in the dataset is hM4Di (Gi).

outcomes.statement: The bestrophin1 inhibitor NPPB lowers SNr spike rate, which the paper takes to suggest that bestrophin1 channels in SNr astrocytes release an excitatory transmitter, not GABA.
outcomes.source: Results, Tonic GABA release was not derived from GPe terminals or astrocytes, paragraph 2; Figure S4C
outcomes.quote: In line with the notion that astrocytes were exciting (not inhibiting) SNr neurons, bath application of the bestrophin1 inhibitor NPPB decreased SNr spiking rate (P = 0.03 and n = 6)
outcomes.notes: No file's notes name NPPB.

outcomes.statement: The D1R antagonist SCH39166 (2 uM) raises SNr spike rate significantly, by a small amount (about 10%).
outcomes.source: Results, Dopamine enhanced tonic GABA release from dSPN terminals, paragraph 1; Figure S2A; Discussion, Tonic GABAergic signaling..., paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Bath application of SCH39166 (2 μM) did significantly elevate SNr spiking rate (P = 0.02 and n = 12) ... the modal change in spiking rate produced by antagonizing D1Rs was small (∼10%)
outcomes.notes: No file's notes name SCH39166 or a D1R antagonist.

outcomes.statement: Quinpirole raises SNr spike rate more than the D1R antagonist does.
outcomes.source: Figure S2B; Results, Dopamine enhanced tonic GABA release from dSPN terminals, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Bath applied D2R agonist elevates SNr firing rate significantly more than bath applied D1R antagonist. Unpaired T-test, n = 8 D2R / 12 D1R, p = 0.03.
outcomes.notes: Depends on figs2a-d1-antagonist-increases-rate, whose SCH39166 recordings are not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: The dendrites of ALDH1A1+ dopaminergic neurons course through much of the dorsoventral extent of the SNr, in rostral and caudal sections.
outcomes.source: Results, SNc dopaminergic neurons directly contributed to tonic GABA release, paragraph 1; Figure 5A and 5B
outcomes.quote: In both rostral and caudal regions, the ... of ALDH1A1+ dopaminergic neurons coursed through much of dorsoventral extent of SNr
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds only intracellular recordings (VoltageClampSeries); no images.

outcomes.statement: SNr neurons from mice with ALDH1A1 knocked down in the SNc by shRNA fire faster than control SNr neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, SNc dopaminergic neurons directly contributed to tonic GABA release, paragraph 2; Figure 5D
outcomes.quote: In ex vivo, cell-attached recordings from SNr neurons, the basal spiking rate was significantly higher than in controls (P < 0.001 and n = 18 control/15 shRNA)
outcomes.notes: The dataset labels no cell as a control of the shRNA experiments, so neither reading of the criterion (the control cells as the dataset labels them, or the 18 control cells of Fig. 5F) can be identified. As a variant only, with untreated gabazine-alone cells as stand-ins, the 15 shRNA cells (26.4 Hz) are faster than the 31 episodic cells (20.3 Hz, Welch P = 0.029), the 6 of November 2022 (17.2 Hz, P = 0.035) and all 49 (21.4 Hz, P = 0.064; P = 0.038 at threshold 6 and 0.14 at 12); the episodic and November subsets were chosen after the data had been looked at. The paper's P < 0.001 is not approached. Question for the authors: which 18 control cells form Fig. 5D (and 5F)?

outcomes.statement: In SNr neurons from ALDH1A1 shRNA mice, gabazine does not significantly change the basal spike rate.
outcomes.source: Results, SNc dopaminergic neurons directly contributed to tonic GABA release, paragraph 2; Figure 5E
outcomes.quote: Moreover, bath application of gabazine did not significantly change the basal spiking rate of SNr neurons from ALDH1A1 shRNA treated mice (P = 0.05 and n = 15)
outcomes.notes: In the 15 shRNA cells gabazine gives 26.4 against 25.7 Hz, paired t test P = 0.78 under both readings, -2.5% (mean of cells); P >= 0.63 at every threshold. Without the failed recording 7084-2022-11-28-73 (14 cells) P >= 0.084, +3.7% at threshold 8, reading a.
deviations: Spike detection is a threshold of 8 robust noise units on the 300 Hz high-passed current with a 4 ms dead time, a choice made here where the paper gives no settings (claims file, M1); every rate result is also shown at 6 and 12.
The drug's application time is not in the files; reading (b) of M1 counts the 6 min from the start of the file the notes say the drug was applied in.

Seven cell-attached recordings lose their action currents during the experiment (the rate falls under a quarter of the condition before, a limit chosen here, and the spike amplitude falls to the noise). They are kept in the main test, as the claims file asks for every cell, and the test is also run without them.

outcomes.statement: SNr neurons in slices pretreated with the aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitors DEAB or disulfiram fire faster than control neurons.
outcomes.source: Figure 5F
outcomes.quote: Example trace and summary data of SNr spiking from control neurons and neurons pretreated with ALDH1A1 antagonists DEAB or disulfiram. Welch's t test, n = 18 control/18 blocked, P < 0.01.
outcomes.notes: The control cells are not labelled in the dataset, as for fig5d-shrna-higher-rate. As a variant only: the 18 cells recorded in DEAB or disulfiram (8 DEAB only, 5 DEAB then gabazine, 3 disulfiram then gabazine, 2 with disulfiram applied during the recording), the paper's n, fire at 20.3 Hz; untreated gabazine-alone stand-ins fire at 21.4 Hz (all 49, Welch P = 0.59), 20.3 Hz (31 episodic, P = 0.99) and 17.2 Hz (6 of November 2022, P = 0.39). The treated cells are not faster against any stand-in set or threshold.

outcomes.statement: In slices treated with disulfiram (10 uM), gabazine no longer changes SNr spike rate.
outcomes.source: Results, SNc dopaminergic neurons directly contributed to tonic GABA release, paragraph 3; Figure 5G
outcomes.quote: Disulfiram blocked the effect of gabazine (P = 0.40 and n = 5)
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 3 disulfiram-then-gabazine cells, all from one mouse, against the paper's 5. Gabazine gives 18.8 against 10.5 Hz, paired t test P = 0.27 (reading b P = 0.19), P >= 0.19 at every threshold; the rate falls in all 3, by 43% on average, in one to 0 Hz. That cell, 6808-2022-05-31-45, is a failed recording; without it the 2 cells give P >= 0.45. The test has little power: for a rise of the paper's gabazine size (25% of the mean basal rate, with the spread of the change in the gabazine-alone cells) a paired t test finds it with probability 0.25 with 3 cells and 0.58 with 5, so the absence found here carries little weight.

outcomes.statement: Activating Gi-DREADD in SNc dopaminergic neurons of DAT-Cre mice with CNO slows their spiking, by 19% on average.

findings.statement: The condition of each recording (virus, drugs, which file is the control and which the drug, when the drug was applied, measurement windows) is given only in free-text NWB `notes`, in many spellings. The files have no icephys tables, intervals or other structured condition labels, and the light and electrical stimuli are not stored (the stimulus series hold only a -10 mV test pulse), so stimulus times must be read from the responses.

Notes that do not match their files: the nine files 0015 to 0023 of subject 9019 (an optogenetic IPSC cell) carry the notes of files 0003 to 0010 of the same day, so which of them were recorded in quinpirole is not stated; file 0007 of subject 8952 and file 0000 of subject 6813 (Five stim) are not named in their own notes.
Sixteen files are deposited twice: each pair has the same session id with different `obj-` suffixes and the same first sweep (subjects 4981, 4982, 4983, 4984, 5011, 5012, 9045).

Seven cell-attached recordings lose their action currents during the experiment: the spike amplitude shrinks to the noise and the rate falls to under a quarter of the condition before (cells of subjects 5110, 6808, 6812, 7084, 7310, 7324 and 8797). An eighth, 8979-2025-05-27-164, shrinks to the noise in the same way, though its rate falls only to 26% of the condition before. In some the amplitude starts to fall in the control file. Nothing in the files marks these recordings, and they sit in the dataset beside the others.

Subject ids 6806, 6813 and 7321 have recordings on dates 4, 32 and 7 days apart, with ages that advance with the date. Slice experiments are terminal, so either the ids were reused or the dates are wrong.

The notes give 30 C for all 412 files, where the paper's Methods give 32 to 33 C, and holding potentials of -50, -55 and -70 mV for the optogenetic IPSC cells, where the paper gives -60 mV. The Fig. S4E legend also says 30 C.

The dataset holds no SNc recordings (Fig. S3), no recordings with SCH39166 (Fig. S2), NPPB or Gq-DREADD (Fig. S4B, C), gabazine then quinpirole (Fig. 3D), low glucose (Fig. S8) or room temperature (Fig. S4D, E), no evoked IPSCs in gabazine (Fig. 1B), and none of the imaging, RNAscope, PercevalHR or voltammetry data. Sixteen claims are blocked for missing data, one of them (fig6c) only through its dependency on the SNc recordings; its own SNr recordings are present.

Counts differ from the paper's: 49 gabazine-alone cells against 45 (Fig. 3B legend), 10 (Results) and 39 (Fig. S1); 3 disulfiram-then-gabazine cells against 5 (Fig. 5G); 7 quinpirole cells without an opsin against 8 (Fig. 3A). No cell is labelled as a control of the shRNA or inhibitor experiments (Fig. 5D, 5F).

Questions for the authors. (1) The spike detection settings in Clampfit and how the stable window of each condition was chosen; the significance of three outcomes here changes with the detection threshold. (2) Which 18 control cells form Fig. 5D and 5F. (3) Which 8 cells form Fig. 3A: the Fig. 2 Chronos cells before the train, or the cells recorded without an opsin, which here do not speed up in quinpirole.
The dandiset's related resource is the bioRxiv preprint; the published paper (doi:10.1126/sciadv.adq8840) is not linked.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier read the general/notes of every asset over HTTP to check the blocked claims, and tested the helpers on synthetic data. It found no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. Of its ten problems, the five marked as affecting a conclusion were answered in the notebook: fig6c's test is run (kept blocked by its dependency), the threshold-sensitive and collapsing cells are shown and each affected claim is run without the seven failed recordings, fig2c is run under reading b of M1, fig4a is measured on clean sweeps, and fig5d and fig5f are blocked as metadata_insufficient. Of the others: fig5g's power is computed (6); the drug application time is still taken as the start of the drug's file and the control of reading b still uses all control episodes, as stated in the helper (7); the gap-free files are printed by cell with the gap after the cell's previous file, 5 to 80 s (8); file 0023 of subject 9019 is measured (9); the protocol-name classification needed no change (10). Report in transcripts/simmons-2026/verifier-1-report.md.

disagreements.reason: Blocked, metadata_insufficient. Neither control reading in the criterion can be identified. With gabazine-alone baselines standing in as controls, the shRNA cells are faster with Welch P = 0.029–0.14, against the paper's < 0.001. Problem 5: the controls are a stand-in the author chose; subsets (ii) episodic and (iii) Nov 2022 were picked after looking at the data; it is stated as an assumption but is not a reading the criterion allows.

Blocked by the attempt, but testable. The archive holds the 8 SNr cells (DAT-Cre, DIO-hM4Di, 10 µM CNO), matching n = 8. The notebook computed their rates and never ran the test, so no outcome can be given (problem 1).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 39 outcomes and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. It asked that the assumptions of fig3b and fig4b be stated as such, found eight places where the text did not match the printed outputs, and left two round-1 points open: 8979-2025-05-27-164, now shown to be a failed recording with both fig7f claims run without it, and the drug application time of 8945-2025-04-16-144, now shown not to affect fig3b. No outcome changes and none is proposed. Report in transcripts/simmons-2026/verifier-2-report.md.

entries.name: simmons-2026
entries.title: Tonic GABA and its dopaminergic modulation in the SNr (Simmons et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the slice electrophysiology findings of Simmons et al. (2026) on dandiset 001777, which holds cell-attached recordings of SNr neurons before and after bath drugs and whole-cell evoked IPSCs. It compares spike rates and IPSC amplitudes across quinpirole, gabazine, DREADD, ALDH1A1 knockdown and inhibitors, rasagiline and GABA transporter blockers. The SNc recordings, imaging, RNAscope and voltammetry of the paper are not in the dandiset.
